newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end flat to up 1/4.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end flat to up 1/4.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond prices ended flat to up 1/4 point, while Bear Stearns & Co cut yields on a New York Local Government Assistance Corp deal and increased its size to $500 million.

"There seems to be a lot of demand for new issues, and not so much demand for secondary bonds," one trader said, citing what he called "a real uncoupling" of those sectors evident both Tuesday and over the past few weeks.
"I think that's because of the characteristics of the bonds. (There is) a lot of '03, '04 call paper in the Street which doesn't have big demand."
Meanwhile strong demand exists "serially a long the line from insurance companies," and new issues are commanding good prices.

"You can probably buy secondary bonds anywhere from five to 10 (basis points) cheaper than you can in the new issue market," the trader said. Secondary prices ended flat to quoted up slightly, he said.
A municipal analyst said prices were up 1/4 point overall, with high-grade issues improving by two basis points overall, and by three basis points in spots. Dollar bonds closed up 1/4 point.
Secondary activity was light and new issue pricing was "very solid, not aggressive, but right there," he said.

In new issues, Bear Stearns increased the LGAC deal to $500 million from $385 million. The deal was restructured and repriced, with yields lowered in several maturities. The top yield in 2019 was cut to 5.65 percent from 5.675 percent.
Also Tuesday, BA Securities Inc priced $340.6 million San Francisco State Building Authority lease revenue bonds. The bonds were priced at a top yield of 5.59 percent in 2021.
On the competitive side, J.P. Morgan won $131.5 million San Francisco City and County, Calif., Airports Commission bonds at a 7.2604 percent true interest cost.
Smith Barney Inc won $118.5 million San Francisco airport bonds, subject to the alternative minimum tax, at a 5.809 percent TIC.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed down 14/32 at 100-27/32 to yield 6.44 percent. In debt futures, the December municipal contract closed up 6/32 at 117-4/32. The December T-bond contract closed up 12/32 at 115-7/32. The MOB spread was 61 ticks.
